HOSPITAL CONNECT

About Us

Helping EMS and hospitals stay in touch.

EMS crews need to know which hospital can help before they arrive. That can be difficult when an emergency room closes or a hospital is short on staff.

We’re building Hospital Connect to make resource requests easier to follow, with the needs of rural communities in British Columbia in mind.

A FIRST-HAND PERSPECTIVE

What a BC paramedic shared

WY

William Yeung

Paramedic in British Columbia

Our teammate Lee interviewed William about the challenges crews face on the job.

William described what happens between an emergency call and a hospital handoff. When a hospital takes over care, the crew can get back to responding to calls in the community.

01

Finding out what’s available

William said crews may not know whether a hospital has beds or a trauma team available until they arrive. Dispatchers face the same gap in information.

02

Longer trips, longer shifts

He described how rural emergency room closures can mean longer trips. A 12-hour shift can stretch by another 3–6 hours, bringing crews close to the 16-hour driving limit he described.

03

Waiting to hand over care

William described waits of 1–2 hours before a patient’s first assessment. Crews can spend more time caring for patients in hallways while they wait to hand over care.

04

Updates that are hard to read on the road

Crews cannot always read dispatch messages while driving or caring for a patient. William explained that this can leave them without updates when they need to decide where to go.

05

Systems that don’t share information

William described hospitals using separate computer systems. Information used to arrange transfers between facilities does not always give emergency dispatchers the current hospital status they need.

WHAT WE’RE WORKING ON

Know which hospital accepted

With Hospital Connect, EMS sends a request for a medical resource. A hospital accepts, and the EMS desk sees that hospital’s name and acceptance time.

We still need to test with healthcare teams whether this approach helps reduce delays in practice.

Try the prototype

The app currently uses invented hospital locations and capacity. It is a shared public prototype, not a live emergency service. Please keep real patient information out of it.

Hospital capacity and care arrangements must be confirmed directly with the receiving team.
